model: Retirement-services and insurance FCFE (free capital flow) at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation $109.9M; FY2024 $108.7M; FY2023 $99.4M). PFG publishes no combined equity-award-tax figure in the XBRL set, so the cash-flow add-back is used alone; net-share-settlement withholding is immaterial against $1.9bn of operating earnings.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 acquisition of treasury stock $902.7M (cash flow statement); H1-2026 $492.7M. FY2026 guidance $0.8-1.1bn of repurchases inside $1.5-1.8bn total capital deployment. Buybacks are the mechanism that keeps the count flat; they are value-neutral in this model because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; no newer print on 2026-10-02 before the open)
inputs.share_count_basis: 214,104,641 common shares outstanding at July 22, 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover) plus 2.8M dilutive securities from the Q2 2026 EPS note (2.0M RSUs, 0.5M options, 0.3M performance shares) = 216.9M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows via sbc_pct_path, and PFG's $0.8-1.1bn/yr repurchase programme more than covers grant dilution, so charging dilution on top would count the cost twice. The Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column is weighted-average diluted (220.3M for Q1 2026) and was not used as the divisor.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 9.5% for a USD-denominated US retirement/asset-management/insurance group: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.05-1.10 (fee revenue is equity-market-linked and the spread book is rate-sensitive, so PFG is somewhat higher-beta than a pure life/health underwriter such as GL at 9.0%). This is not a WACC: the flows are post-interest free capital flow (corporate interest on $4.3bn of holdco notes sits inside the Corporate segment loss and therefore inside the pre-tax operating margin). Same rate in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases are immaterial for a financial-services group; no lease adjustment in flows or bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest ($35.0M at 30 June 2026; NCI share of net income $70.4M in FY2025, mostly consolidated sponsored funds) is excluded by construction: non-GAAP operating earnings are attributable to PFG, so the margin path is attributable-only and no NCI deduction is made in the bridge (charged once).
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Holdco debt of $4,340.6M at 30 June 2026 (long-term $4,324.4M incl. the $400M 5.3% 2037 notes issued 1 June 2026 to pre-fund the $350M 3.1% November 2026 maturity, plus $16.2M short-term) is serviced inside the flows: corporate interest expense is inside the Corporate segment loss that non-GAAP pre-tax operating earnings is stated after. Deducting it again after capitalising a post-interest stream would count it twice. Consolidated cash of $944.0M, the $113bn investment portfolio and policy reserves are operating items of the insurance subsidiaries, not net cash, so `cash` is recorded at 0. The $1.6bn of excess and available capital above the 400% RBC target ($2,562.7M of cash and liquid assets at the holding companies at 30 June 2026) is NOT added in the bridge: it is the buffer that funds the Beam Benefits acquisition (closed 1 Sept 2026, price undisclosed) and the deployment guidance above the free-capital-flow run-rate, and crediting it would be the same double-count the GL and IAG.AX builds avoided. It is listed under key risks as upside the model does not credit.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a retirement-services / asset-management / benefits-and-protection group, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net debt at zero (the GL / IAG.AX / GMG.AX / CHC.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent). The dcf-methods routing default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because (1) GAAP equity is not a usable compounding base: at 30 June 2026 it carries a -$4,065.8M AOCI unrealised-loss position and a +$2,137.9M cumulative funds-withheld embedded-derivative gain that move with rates and spreads, and the company itself reports ROE on equity ex both items ($12,531.8M, BVPS $58.40); and (2) PFG does not compound book -- it converts 75-85% of non-GAAP operating earnings to free capital flow and returns it (FY2025: $1,586.7M of buybacks and dividends against $1,866.5M of operating earnings; equity ex-AOCI grew only $12,144.0M -> $12,531.8M over 18 months), so the value driver is the distributable free capital flow, i.e. FCFE. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = GAAP total revenues (FY2025 $15,625.5M; TTM 2Q26 $15,693.2M; this line includes net realised capital losses and exited-business noise, which is why growth is modelled modestly against a rising margin rather than at the operating-EPS rate); ebitda_margin_path = non-GAAP pre-tax operating earnings BEFORE stock compensation as % of revenue (TTM 2Q26: $2,405.1M pre-tax operating + $109.9M SBC = 16.0%; FY2025 ~15.3%; year-1 base 16.2% is what the 9-12% EPS guidance implies for FY2026 once ~3.5% share shrink is stripped out: $8.55 x 1.09-1.12 = $9.32-9.58 x ~218.5M avg diluted = $2.04-2.09bn after tax, $2.5bn pre-tax, $2.6bn before SBC, on ~$16.2bn revenue); sbc_pct_path charges SBC (0.70% of revenue, drifting to 0.65%); da_pct_path = 0 (D&A is immaterial; 'capex' here is not PP&E); capex_pct_path = statutory capital RETAINED in the subsidiaries to hold RBC ~400% and fund new-business strain -- the complement of the 75-85% free-capital-flow conversion guidance -- calibrated at 2.5% of revenue in year 1 (~20% of NOPAT, i.e. 80% conversion, year-1 FCFE ~$1.64bn vs FY2026 deployment guidance of $1.5-1.8bn) and tapering to 2.2% as revenue growth and capital strain slow; cash_tax_rate_path = the non-GAAP operating effective tax rate (TTM 2Q26 18.3%; guided 17-20%) held at 18.5% -- cash taxes paid were only $220.7M in FY2025 against ~$440M of book operating tax on reserve/DAC timing differences, and that shelter is deliberately NOT perpetuated. last_fcf is FY2025 free capital flow at 80% conversion of $1,866.5M non-GAAP operating earnings (~$1,493M; capital actually returned $1,586.7M), NOT reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income: an insurer's operating cash flow ($4,536.7M, dominated by policyholder deposits and investment activity) is not free cash, so that identity is deliberately not satisfied here. UNMODELLED CORPORATE ACTIONS: Beam Benefits (closed 1 Sept 2026, consideration undisclosed, ~25,000 SMB customers) and DentaNet (March 2026) are inside the base margin path only through the Benefits and Protection margin expansion; the Chile annuities runoff sale to Banco Santander (expected close Q3 2026, proceeds undisclosed) is a small capital release not credited. Both nets are assumed to roughly offset.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case ten-year average revenue growth: 3.5-4.0% near term (FY2026 operating-EPS guidance of 9-12% less ~3.5% share shrink implies 5-8% earnings growth, delivered through margin expansion on a 3.5-4% revenue line, plus Beam Benefits from Sept 2026) decelerating to 2.5% terminal. GAAP revenue history is not the anchor because it embeds net realised capital gains/losses and exited-business reinsurance accounting (FY2022 $17.5bn, FY2023 $13.7bn).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP equity CAGRs are meaningless for PFG: AOCI swung from +$1.6bn (FY2020) to -$5.3bn (FY2023) on rates and equity fell $16.6bn -> $10.0bn across FY2020-22 while the business grew, so the 3yr +6.0% and 5yr -6.4% equity CAGRs diverge from revenue (-3.8%/+1.2%) and EPS (-34.5%/+0.9%) by far more than 30%. EPS CAGRs are distorted by the FY2022 $4.8bn GAAP net income (gain on the Talcott retail-fixed-annuity/ULSG reinsurance exit) and by FY2023/FY2025 exited-business losses. Growth was selected from guidance and the non-GAAP operating series, not from any GAAP CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_5yr_cagr is on capital RETURNED to shareholders (buybacks + common dividends, the realised owner stream): FY2020 $307.0M + $618M = ~$925M -> FY2025 $902.7M + $684.0M = $1,586.7M. fcf_3yr_cagr is null because the FY2022 base ($1,661.1M of buybacks funded by the Talcott reinsurance proceeds) is not a comparable run-rate. Reported FCF (operating cash flow $3.2-4.6bn, no capex line) is an insurer's operating cash flow and is not the owner series; it was not used for any CAGR. Non-GAAP operating EPS ex-significant-variances: FY2024 $7.65 -> FY2025 $8.55 (+11.8%); H1-2026 $4.59 vs $3.99 (+15%). BVPS ex-AOCI and funds-withheld derivative: $53.69 (FY2024) -> $58.40 (2Q26), +8.8% in 18 months.

base.narrative: Revenue grows 3.5-4% near term (recordkeeping fee growth on AUA of $1.9tn, ~$3bn/yr of PRT premium, International Pension AUM growth, Beam Benefits from Sept 2026) decelerating to 2.5%; pre-SBC pre-tax operating margin rises from 16.2% (FY2026 guidance-implied) to 17.0% as RIS margin reaches the top of its 38-41% range and the mix shifts toward fee and capital-light businesses; retained capital tapers from 2.5% to 2.2% of revenue (free capital flow conversion ~80% -> ~83%) as growth slows; operating tax 18.5%; terminal at min(Gordon 9.5%/2.5% = 14.6x, 13x FCFE cap) -- the cap binds.

bull.narrative: Equity markets and DC flows compound AUA, PRT stays a $3bn+/yr franchise with repeat clients, Principal Asset Management net outflows reverse, International Pension (Brazil, Mexico, Chile) keeps double-digit AUM growth, and Beam/DentaNet lift Benefits and Protection margins; revenue grows 5-5.5% for three years and the pre-SBC pre-tax operating margin reaches 18%; capital-light mix lets retained capital fall to 1.9% of revenue (conversion ~85%); terminal growth 3.0%, cap 15x FCFE. Even here the exit is a mature-financial multiple, not a growth re-rating.

bear.narrative: A rate-cut cycle compresses the spread book and raises GMWB hedging cost while an equity drawdown cuts fee revenue on $1.9tn of AUA; asset-management outflows persist (Q2-2026 ran ~$11bn), fee compression from Fidelity/Vanguard/Empower bites in SMB recordkeeping, PRT volumes fall with lower rates, and a CRE/commercial-mortgage credit cycle lifts regulatory capital retention to 2.5-2.8% of revenue (conversion ~75%); revenue growth fades to 1-2%, margin drifts to 14.5%, tax 19.5%; the stock de-rates to 10x FCFE. No solvency event: RBC 406% and $1.6bn of excess capital keep this a margin-and-multiple bear, not a going-concern one.

scenario_narratives.base: PFG keeps doing what it did in FY2025: mid-single-digit operating-earnings growth from recordkeeping fees, PRT, International Pension and benefits, turned into 9-12% EPS growth by ~3-4%/yr of share shrink, with 75-85% of operating earnings converted to free capital flow and returned. Value is the FCFE stream at a 9.5% cost of equity capped at 13x in the terminal year; GAAP book value, distorted by AOCI and the funds-withheld derivative, is a cross-check (BVPS ex-AOCI $58.40 at 2Q26; the price is ~1.9x that and ~11.7x FY2026 guided operating EPS), not the model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Markets and flows cooperate: AUA compounds, PRT and International Pension grow double digits, Principal Asset Management outflows reverse, Beam/DentaNet lift the benefits franchise, and the capital-light mix lets conversion run at the top of the 75-85% range. Revenue grows 5-5.5% for three years, the pre-SBC pre-tax operating margin reaches 18%, and the exit is 15x FCFE -- still a mature-financial multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two 'high' severity risks in the Analysis -- the rate cycle and equity-market sensitivity -- land together: spread compression and higher hedging cost on the retirement book, fee revenue down with markets, asset-management outflows that never reverse, PRT demand fading with lower rates, and a CRE credit cycle that keeps more capital in the subsidiaries. Growth fades to 1-2%, margin to 14.5%, conversion to ~75%, and the stock de-rates to 10x FCFE. Solvency is not the issue (RBC 406%); the multiple and the margin are.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20% because the two highest-severity risks in the Analysis (rate cycle, equity-market sensitivity) are macro factors PFG cannot control and both act on earnings in the same direction, and Principal Asset Management is already in net outflow; not raised further because the balance sheet carries no solvency or refinancing risk (RBC 406%, $1.6bn excess capital, next maturity pre-funded). Bull cut from 35% to 30% because it needs several independent things at once -- market appreciation, an outflow reversal, sustained PRT and international growth, and clean Beam integration. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Principal is valued as the present value of the free capital flow its holding company can actually distribute -- 75-85% of non-GAAP operating earnings after the statutory capital the insurance subsidiaries must retain -- discounted at a 9.5% cost of equity with no separate net-debt deduction, because corporate interest is already inside the operating margin. GAAP book value was rejected as the compounding base (AOCI -$4.1bn, funds-withheld derivative +$2.1bn, and the company returns rather than retains) but serves as a cross-check: at 30 June 2026 BVPS ex-AOCI was $58.40, growing ~6%/yr net of buybacks; a 1.7x exit P/B on year-5 BVPS-ex-AOCI (~$78) discounted at 9.5% plus five years of dividends (~$3.4-4.2/share/yr) lands around $100-105, in the same neighbourhood as the FCFE base case. The terminal is capped at 13x FCFE in base (10x bear, 15x bull), inside the 11.7x forward operating P/E the market pays today.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital-retention assumption (capex_pct 2.5% -> 2.2% of revenue, i.e. 80-83% free capital flow conversion) is the single most important driver: every 1pp of revenue retained permanently is roughly $10/share; it is calibrated to the 75-85% guidance band that FY2025 delivered at the top of

Pre-SBC pre-tax operating margin path (16.2% -> 17.0%) rests on RIS reaching the top of its 38-41% range and Benefits and Protection absorbing Beam Benefits accretively; each 0.5pp of permanent margin is ~$4-5/share

$1.6bn of excess and available capital (~$7/share) and the Chile annuities sale proceeds are NOT credited in the bridge; the Beam Benefits consideration (undisclosed, closed 1 Sept 2026) is likewise not deducted -- the two are assumed to roughly offset

Rates and markets: fee revenue on $1.9tn AUA and spread income on the general account move with equities and the curve; the bear case models both adverse together and is still a 10x-multiple outcome, not a solvency one
Operating tax rate held at the 18.5% book rate while cash taxes paid were ~half that in FY2025; if the reserve/DAC timing shelter persists the model is conservative by several dollars a share

GAAP revenue line (the engine's growth base) embeds net realised capital gains/losses and exited-business reinsurance effects; a year of large realised losses would make the margin path look wrong without the underlying operating earnings having moved

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 77.90-121.18
